citation.title: Self-directed online machine learning for topology optimization
citation.authors: Changyu Deng, Yizhou Wang, Can Qin, Yun Fu, Wei Lu
citation.version_coded: open-access version of record; queue title was an earlier title of arXiv 2002.01927

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Across its test problems, online surrogate optimization is said to cut computation by roughly two to five orders of magnitude relative to direct heuristic optimization.
claim.key_phrase: reduced the computational time by 2 ~ 5 orders of magnitude
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Abstract, p. 1: two to five orders of magnitude means approximately 100 to 100,000 times; the numeric field records the stated lower endpoint. Discussion, p. 10 clarifies much of this is estimated FE-evaluation reduction.
claim.alternatives: Results, pp. 4-5: 501 versus estimated 200,000 FE calculations (400-fold) for coarse compliance, and 10,243 versus estimated 4 million (about 400-fold) for fine compliance; Discussion, p. 10 reports 2-4 orders for truss cases.

baseline.classical_method: Abstract/Results: directly applied GSA for compliance, BBA for fluid, and BA for truss; an MMA benchmark is also shown for compliance (Figures 2-3).
baseline.implementation: Methods, FEM and gradient-based baselines: COMSOL Multiphysics 5.4 computes FE objectives and MMA; Methods also specify heuristic algorithms. Public MATLAB/Python code is deposited per Code availability.
baseline.problem_size: Discussion, p. 9: compliance examples have 25 and 121 continuous design variables; fluid examples 160 and 640 binary variables; truss examples 72, 432 and 1008 bars (Figure 7).
baseline.classical_iterations: Results, compliance pp. 4-5: direct GSA estimated at 200,000 and 4,000,000 objective/FE evaluations for coarse and fine problems; no matched observed stopping count stated.
baseline.training_time: Discussion, p. 10: online DNN training overhead described as almost negligible, with time profile in Supplementary Table 1; no main-text duration stated.
baseline.data_generation_cost: Results and Discussion, pp. 4-5, 9: online FE calls are included as 501 for coarse compliance and 10,243 for fine compliance; no separate offline dataset.
baseline.quality_metric: Results, compliance pp. 4-5: FE-computed dimensionless elastic energy; Fig. 2 reports returned design energy and volume constraint; other cases use pressure, charging time and truss weight.
baseline.quality_gap: Results, compliance pp. 4-5: coarse SOLO energy 0.298 at 501 FE evaluations versus MMA benchmark 0.293 (about 1.7% higher [inferred]); fine SOLO 0.228 versus MMA 0.222 (about 2.7% higher [inferred]).

R1.evidence: Abstract and compliance Results, pp. 4-5: headline speed range aggregates different tasks; compliance outputs have FE-reported objective but are above MMA benchmark, and direct GSA costs are estimated without a matched-quality observed run.

R2.evidence: Abstract, p. 1, emphasizes direct heuristic baselines; compliance Results, pp. 4-5, also show MMA reaching lower FE-computed energy, but do not compare SOLO speed against that stronger classical optimizer.

R3.evidence: Results algorithm and Discussion, pp. 3 and 10: DNN is trained online from FE calls for each optimization; there is no offline amortized training set.

R4.evidence: Methods, FEM and volume constraint, pp. 10-11: returned designs are scored by FE and volume is enforced for compliance; no aggregate rate of infeasible or failed designs is given.

reporting.n_test_cases: Introduction/Discussion, pp. 2 and 9: 8 problems total; 6 in-scope examples (2 compliance, 1 heat, 3 truss) and 2 fluid examples outside this audit's physics scope.

notes: The queue's historical title is an earlier title of arXiv 2002.01927; the accessible Nature Communications version of record is coded. The paper includes fluid examples, but also includes in-scope solid compliance and thermal optimization. Its public repository has the example code and an MIT license; the truss benchmark is Python-only, while compliance uses COMSOL/MATLAB. The main speed range largely reflects estimated FE-call ratios, and the Discussion distinguishes estimated from observed direct heuristic tests.
